questions.question: A clinic has a low rate of timely follow-up after newly uncontrolled hypertension. What is the best first QI step?
choices: Install a new alert immediately
Define the affected population, verify baseline performance, map the current process, and include patient and staff perspectives
Discipline clinicians below the average
Measure only blood pressure at the end of the year
questions.explanation: Improvement begins with a clearly defined problem and understanding of the current system; selecting a solution before examining the workflow can optimize the wrong process.

questions.question: Which measure is a balancing measure for a project that adds rapid follow-up appointments?
choices: Percentage of eligible patients offered follow-up
Mean systolic blood pressure at three months
Urgent-message turnaround time and staff overtime after the scheduling change
Number of examination rooms
questions.explanation: Balancing measures detect unintended consequences elsewhere, such as workload or delays created by the new appointment process.

questions.question: Which statement is the best example of a specific improvement aim?
choices: Increase 30-day follow-up for adults with newly uncontrolled hypertension in Clinic A from 52% to 75% by December 31 without worsening urgent-message turnaround
Improve hypertension care soon
Make every patient compliant
Add reminder calls
questions.explanation: A strong aim defines the population, setting, baseline, target, deadline, and an important safety or balancing condition without prescribing the solution.

questions.question: What should the team do in the Study phase of a PDSA cycle?
choices: Permanently mandate the change
Choose a project title
Repeat the Plan step without collecting data
Compare observations and data with the prediction, identify learning, and decide what should change
questions.explanation: Study means analyzing what happened against the prediction and extracting learning that informs adoption, adaptation, or abandonment.

questions.question: Which statement about run charts is most accurate?
choices: They prove causation from any change
They display data in time order to help detect shifts, trends, and sustainment when interpreted with defined rules and context
They replace operational definitions
They require every data point to be explained as a special cause
questions.explanation: Time-ordered data help distinguish patterns from isolated pre/post differences, but a run chart alone does not prove causation.

questions.question: A harmful medication event is being reviewed. Which corrective action is generally stronger than education alone?
choices: Tell staff to be more careful
Send the same policy again
Redesign the ordering interface to prevent selection of the unsafe dose and monitor the effect
Post a warning sign without changing workflow
questions.explanation: System redesign and forcing constraints reduce reliance on memory and vigilance and are generally stronger than reminders, policies, or education used alone.

questions.question: Which response best reflects Just Culture?
choices: Examine behavior, intent, system conditions, incentives, and available choices, then match redesign, coaching, or accountability to the findings
Never hold an individual accountable
Automatically punish any person closest to the event
Keep events confidential from the safety team
questions.explanation: Just Culture balances systems learning with fair accountability; it is neither blame-free nor automatic punishment.

questions.question: How does FMEA differ most clearly from root cause analysis?
choices: FMEA is used only after a sentinel event
RCA is always prospective
FMEA requires no process map
FMEA prospectively examines how a process might fail, while RCA retrospectively investigates an event
questions.explanation: FMEA anticipates failure modes before harm, whereas RCA reconstructs and analyzes an event that occurred; both should lead to risk-reduction actions.

questions.question: A screening alert increases orders, but completion remains lower for patients without portal access. What is the best response?
choices: Report the overall order rate only
Stratify completion, engage affected patients, add accessible outreach pathways, and monitor referral capacity and workload
Exclude patients without portal access from the denominator
Conclude the project is successful because alerts fired
questions.explanation: Equitable improvement measures who completes the care pathway, identifies access gaps, co-designs alternatives, and watches for burden and capacity problems.

questions.question: What is the FNP's first priority after discovering a patient safety event that may have caused harm?
choices: Wait until the monthly quality meeting
Edit the original record to remove the error
Assess and protect the patient, escalate through approved clinical and safety channels, document facts accurately, and support timely communication
Determine who should be disciplined before examining the patient
questions.explanation: Immediate patient assessment and harm mitigation come first, followed by accurate documentation, required escalation and reporting, and transparent communication under local policy and law.
